messages:
Nathan: Dropping an nsys + perfetto capture for the regression hitting tail latencies when long sequences (8k) are present. link: https://perf.internal/reports/1816782345

Sara: Looked at the nsys. Multiple H2D memcpy bursts coincide with repeated KV-cache evictions. Perfetto shows periodic HBM bandwidth spikes and stalled kernels around the same timeline windows.

Mike: I repro on A100-80GB. The coalescer is combining mixed seq lengths (e.g., 512 + 8192) into single microbatches. Kernel selector picks the fast_small_seq path initially but then falls back to attention_blocked for the >4k rows. blocked path costs ~2.5-3x for these shapes.

Alex: Is this the coalescer change we rolled two weeks ago? We intentionally mixed sequences to boost utilization but maybe missed pathological long-seq cases.

Jin: Confirmed. Recent coalescing increases average throughput but creates microbatches dominated by extremes that choose suboptimal kernels. Also prefetch logic is overly aggressive for large-stride KV access patterns which thrashes page churn.

Nathan: Initial mitigation idea: add a guard so we don't coalesce sequences >4096 with other lengths, and tune KV prefetch window. Suggested env flags to test: COALESCE_SEQ_LIMIT=4096, KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=4, KV_PAGE_PIN=true.

Mike: Quick local test: COALESCE_SEQ_LIMIT=4096 cuts tail latency back to baseline and HBM BW drops from ~700GB/s to ~430GB/s sustained. Eviction counters in the trace decrease substantially.

Jin: Another finding: the runtime image lost a compiler optimization flag in a recent Docker patch (-fno-tree-vectorize accidentally introduced). Rebuilding with -O3 and restoring vectorization speeds up the small-block GEMM used by the fast path, narrowing the gap to the blocked kernel. We'll queue a rebuild.

Sara: Sample profiling command I ran for the capture:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_8k_guard --trace=cuda,cudnn --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --force-overwrite --duration=90 \n  ./run_inference --model rwl-13b --seq-len 8192 --batch 2
```
perf top hot kernels excerpt:
```
attention_blocked_kernel   42%
kv_cache_page_read        16%
cudaMemcpyAsync H2D       14%
small_gemm_kernel          9%
softmax_stable             6%
```

Alex: Proposed two-step hotfix: 1) immediately conservative-coalesce (or set COALESCE_SEQ_LIMIT=4096 by default) to avoid mixed extreme microbatches; 2) rebuild runtime with corrected compile flags and roll a canary.

Nathan: Opened issue INF-2010 and uploaded the traces + perfetto links. Assigning Sara and Mike to run canary with the env toggles and attach nsys + perfetto outputs to INF-2010. If the canary shows regressions we revert coalescer. :thumbsup:

Mike: FYI: enabling KV_PAGE_PIN=true trades higher steady HBM usage for fewer H2D memcpy spikes and much lower tail variance. Might be acceptable for latency-sensitive customers.

Jin: I'll push a runtime rebuild (restore vectorization, -O3, unroll hot loops) and kick off a canary image build. If canary looks good we promote.

perf-bot: Automated alert: HBM bandwidth crossed 600 GB/s threshold on canary cluster at 2026-03-18T15:42:03Z • correlates with INF-2010.

Sara: Starting a fresh canary now with COALESCE_SEQ_LIMIT=4096, KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=4, KV_PAGE_PIN=true. Will drop traces in INF-2010 in ~45m.

Nathan: Good. Also we should prototype a kernel-selection heuristic that estimates FLOPs/memory for the microbatch instead of pure seq-thresholds — might avoid brittle boundaries. If anyone experiments post links in INF-2010.

Mike: On it. I'll try an estimator that computes expected GEMM shapes and picks kernel by expected runtime cost rather than only seq bins.

Nathan: Thanks — tight updates in the issue please.
